title: Etale purity across a regular integral Cartier divisor
statement: Let $L$ be locally Noetherian and $i:D\to L$ an effective Cartier centre [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with $D$ regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $U\subseteq L$ be the open complement of the image of $i$. Let $n:N\to L$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $U$. Suppose $W\subseteq L$ is open, contains the image of the generic point of $D$, and $n$ is etale over $W$. Then there are a finite etale $p:E\to L$ and an isomorphism $N|_U\cong E|_U$ over $U$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or normality of $N$ is assumed.

proof.text: An effective Cartier divisor is nowhere dense, so U is dense. At every point of D, the Noetherian local ring of L has regular quotient by the Cartier nonzerodivisor, so it is regular (Stacks 00NU). At the generic point the quotient is a field and the local ring is a DVR. At other points of the integral D the quotient has positive dimension and the local ring has dimension at least two. Thus the generic point of D is the only codimension-one point of L outside U.

The restriction n over W is finite etale. Restrict further to the DVR at the image of the generic point of D. This finite etale model identifies on the fraction field with the restriction of n over U, so that punctured cover is unramified there. This verifies unramifiedness in codimension one at all points outside U.

Apply Stacks Tag 0EYE to the regular effective Cartier divisor D and the finite etale cover n over U. This gives a finite etale p over L and an isomorphism of restrictions over U. Orient the isomorphism from N to E; the over-U condition is the displayed composition equality. The theorem applies also to the empty cover and requires only local Noetherianity.
